newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks mixed in morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks mixed in morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks were mixed in early trade on Tuesday, pulled up by utilities and down by properties, brokers said.
"No particular share or sector is performing well today," said Francis Wu, institutional sales manager at South China Brokerage.
The Hang Seng Index was up 27 points, or 0.18 percent, to 15,398. Turnover was a robust HK$2.4 billion after 20 minutes.
"Some red chips are looking slightly better," Wu said.
The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index was 37 points, or 1.12 percent, higher at 3,427.

The utility sector continued to outperform the market and banks put on a positive performance. But property shares were generally weaker, still plagued by uncertainties over the new government's policy initiatives, brokers said.
Hongkong Telecom continued its rally, adding HK$0.25 to HK$18.85 and Hongkong Electric jumped HK$0.70 to HK$32.20.
Property giant Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.00 to HK$91.25.
Property developers' earnings have been impressive for some time but growth of that magnitude is disappearing, analysts said.

Trading in Hopewell Holdings was suspended on Tuesday morning. The company has yet to issue a statement, but brokers said market rumours continued to circulate that a large red chip conglomerate was likely to take a stake in one of Hopewell's China projects.
COSCO Pacific soared to HK$19.20 then eased to trade HK$2.45 higher at HK$18.25. Liu Chong Hing Bank added HK$0.20 to HK$24.50.
The companies released details on Tuesday of the deal whereby COSCO will take a 20 percent stake in the bank.
Traders were cautious on the outlook for the overall market.
"The market cooled off yesterday afternoon and it could close a bit lower today," said one trader with a large U.S. house.
The Hang Seng July futures contract was trading 85 points lower at 15,325 and the August contract was 30 points lower at 15,405.
Futures were a good sentiment indicator, the U.S. trader said.
"Futures are the tail not the dog, remember," he added.
